title: Minimum Hours of Training to Win a Competition
summary: You enter a competition with initial energy and experience.
statement: You enter a competition with initial energy and experience. You face opponents in order, needing more energy and experience than each to win. Each win increases your experience but decreases your energy. Before competing, you can train to increase your initial energy or experience. The goal is to find the minimum training hours needed to defeat all opponents.
constraints: Opponents are fought in the given order.
Before each fight, current energy and experience must both be strictly greater than that opponent’s values.
Winning subtracts the opponent energy and adds the opponent experience; training raises either initial stat by one per hour.
hints: Energy training can be computed once from the total energy cost.
Experience must be handled in fight order because each win increases it.
Raise current experience to rival+1 only when needed, record the increase, then add the rival’s experience.
The energy lower bound is necessary and sufficient; each experience adjustment is the minimum that permits the next fight, so delaying or adding more cannot improve the total.
editorial: The energy lower bound is necessary and sufficient; each experience adjustment is the minimum that permits the next fight, so delaying or adding more cannot improve the total.

tests.explanation: Six energy hours and two strategically required experience hours total eight.
Both initial stats already strictly exceed the only opponent, so no training is needed.
